adminDb.title: Database
adminDb.subtitle: Direct CRUD access to every core table. Use with care — there is no soft delete.

help.why: Sometimes you need to fix a row, backfill a value or clean up test data without writing SQL. This screen exposes every main table with the same controls: filter, sort, edit, delete.

what.2: Click a row to edit any non-system field; click + to insert a new row.
what.3: Use the dedicated editors (Quiz, Rating engine) for guided flows — this screen is the raw fallback.

result.1: You can recover from any data hiccup without bothering an engineer.
result.2: All changes are subject to the same RLS as the rest of the app, so referential integrity stays intact.

what.3: Press “Save changes” to commit; foreign-key and check constraints still apply.

result.1: The change is committed to Postgres immediately and is visible in the table list.
result.2: Players and coaches will see the updated data on their next page load wherever {table} is used.

adminQuiz.title: Onboarding quiz
adminQuiz.subtitle: Versions, questions and answer weights for the starting-Elo questionnaire.
adminQuiz.list_subtitle: Active version drives the live onboarding flow. Drafts are isolated until activated.

help.why: The starting Elo is the very first number a new player sees. A bad guess scares people away. By tuning quiz questions and weights here, you make sure the platform meets every newcomer with a fair, friendly estimate.

what.1: Each row is a version of the questionnaire. Only one is active and shown in the public onboarding.
what.2: Click “New draft” to clone the current version (recommended) or start from scratch. Drafts can be edited freely.
what.3: Open a draft to add or remove questions, change wording in three languages and set option weights.
what.4: When the draft looks right, hit “Activate” — the next signup will use it immediately. Old answers stay attached to the version that produced them.

result.1: Newcomers get a starting Elo that matches their real level, so they enjoy their first matches instead of being smashed.
result.2: You can iterate without code: ship a question on Monday, tweak weights on Friday, all from this screen.

help.why: Universal Elo decides who plays whom in a fair match, who lands in the seasonal race, and how big a win feels. This screen is your safe place to evolve those rules — nothing is editable in code.

what.1: Each row is one snapshot of the rating engine. Only one is active and feeds the live system.
what.2: Click “New draft” to clone the active version. Open the draft to change K-factors, multipliers, starting Elo, and seasonal scoring.
what.3: Use the built-in simulator on the editor page to type in two players + a result and see exactly what Elo deltas this draft would produce — no need to play a real match.
what.4: When you are happy, press “Activate”. From that moment on, every new match score and every onboarding quiz uses the new values; the old version stays in history.

result.1: You can fine-tune rating dynamics gradually — e.g. make tournament finals weigh more without breaking friendly matches.
result.2: If a change feels wrong, just clone the previous version, activate it, and you are back to the old behaviour in one click.

helpPage.title: Help & glossary
helpPage.subtitle: How to find a sparring partner, pick a coach and join or host a tournament — quick answers and a glossary.

help.why: Newcomers to club tennis hit the same dozen questions about matches, coaches and tournaments. This page answers them once.

what.1: Quick guides: find an opponent, pick a coach, join a tournament or create one.

result.1: Less back-and-forth with the coach about how things work.

elo.def: A number that estimates your level. Goes up when you beat better players, down when you lose to worse ones.

k_factor.def: How much your Elo can move per match. Higher for new players (more uncertainty), lower for veterans.

provisional.def: Your first 10 matches. K is double, so the system zeroes-in on your real level fast.

starting_elo.def: Your initial rating, computed from a 60-second quiz when you sign up.

tournament_seed.def: Your slot in the bracket based on rating. Higher seeds avoid each other in early rounds.

bye.def: An automatic free pass to the next round when the bracket size doesn't divide evenly.

no_ad.def: Deuce point becomes sudden-death: receiver chooses side, winner takes the game. Saves time.

super_tiebreak.def: First to 10, win by 2 — instead of a full third set.

wo.def: Win awarded when an opponent doesn't show up. Counts for advancement, not for Elo.

match_proposal.def: A friendly-match request between two players. Both sides confirm before Elo updates.

verified_coach.def: Coach with at least 5 published reviews — earns a green Verified badge.

trust_weighted.def: Coach ranking that shrinks high averages with few reviews back toward the global mean.

outbox.def: Internal queue of all emails. The cron worker drains it every few minutes.

q_register.a: Either accept your coach's invitation email, or sign up directly with magic-link / Google.

q_no_invite.q: I don't have an invitation — can I still join?
q_no_invite.a: Yes. Sign up directly, take the starting quiz, and contact a coach via WhatsApp from their public profile.

q_dispute.q: We disagree on the score — what now?
q_dispute.a: Either side can mark the score as disputed. The coach reviews and decides; Elo only updates after that.

q_payment.a: MVP: manual tracking. The coach marks bookings as paid / unpaid / comped. Online payments are coming in Phase 2.

q_cancel.q: How do I cancel a booking?
q_cancel.a: Open My Bookings → Upcoming → Cancel. You can cancel up to 12 h before the session by default.

q_telegram.a: Belarus skews heavily toward WhatsApp. Telegram is a secondary channel — toggle it on in your profile.

q_data.a: Stored on Supabase EU servers. Export & delete on request. We never sell data.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.intro: PlayTennis.by is an open amateur-tennis platform for Belarus. This policy explains what data we collect, how we use it and how you can control it. The iOS and Android apps are a wrapper around the www.playtennis.by website, so this single policy covers both web and mobile apps.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: The PlayTennis.by team is the data controller. For any privacy question, email the address at the bottom of this page.

sections.heading: What data we collect
paragraphs: We only collect what the platform needs to work:
items: Account: your email address and sign-in identifier.
Profile: name, photo (avatar), city or neighborhood, skill level and settings.
Gameplay data: matches, results, rating, tournament participation and coach reviews.
Location: only if you allow it — to show nearby courts, coaches and players on the map.
Technical data: anonymized usage analytics (pages, events) via PostHog.
Support requests: the message text and the contact you reached us from.

sections.heading: Sign in with Google and Apple
paragraphs: You can sign in by email (magic link) or with Google or Apple. When you use a provider, we receive your email and name to create your account. Sign in with Apple may use "Hide My Email" — in that case we work with the relay address Apple provides. We never see or store your OAuth passwords.

sections.heading: How we use data
items: Create and operate your account and profile.
Match you with opponents, coaches and tournaments at your level and area.
Calculate ratings and show match statistics.
Send service emails (confirmation, match and tournament notifications).
Improve the product using anonymized analytics.
Respond to your support requests.

sections.heading: Data processors (third parties)
paragraphs: We rely on trusted providers that process data on our behalf:
items: Supabase — authentication and database.
Vercel — website hosting.
PostHog — product analytics (anonymized).
Google and Apple — sign-in with the respective accounts.
Resend — sending email.
Telegram — notifications and support if you connect the bot.

sections.heading: Advertising and tracking
paragraphs: We do not sell your data and do not use third-party advertising trackers. PostHog analytics is used only to improve the product and is not linked to ad networks.

sections.heading: Data retention
paragraphs: We keep data while your account exists. After you delete your account, personal data is deleted or anonymized; some records may be retained where required by law or for rating integrity (in anonymized form).

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You can request access, correction or deletion of your data, and withdraw consent. To delete your account and its personal data, email us at the address below — we will handle the request within a reasonable time.

sections.heading: Cookies and session
paragraphs: We use strictly necessary cookies for sign-in and to keep your session. In the mobile apps, the session is stored in the WebView's secure storage.

sections.heading: Children
paragraphs: The platform is not intended for children under 13. We do not knowingly collect children's data.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy. We will note material changes on this page with a new update date.

accountDeletionPage.title: Account Deletion
accountDeletionPage.intro: You can request deletion of your PlayTennis.by account and its personal data at any time. Below is how to submit a request, what is deleted and how long we take to process it.

sections.heading: How to submit a request
paragraphs: Email us from the address linked to your account so we can confirm the request comes from the profile owner.
items: Email: hello@playtennis.by
Subject line: "Account deletion request"
In the message, include the profile name or account email you want deleted
If you signed in with Google or Apple, write from the same address you used to register

sections.heading: What we delete
paragraphs: After we process your request, we delete or anonymize:
items: Your sign-in account (email, OAuth link to Google/Apple)
Profile: name, avatar, city, skill level and settings
Personal contacts and notification preferences
Coach reviews posted under your name
Tournament entries where you are listed as a player
Open matches and applications you created

sections.heading: What may be retained
paragraphs: Some data cannot be fully erased without breaking platform integrity or legal requirements:
items: Completed match results and rating (Elo) history — in anonymized form, with no link to your name or email
Tournament records you took part in — without personal data, only to preserve final draw results
Technical logs and anonymized analytics — with no identifiers that could restore your profile
Data we must keep by law (e.g. accounting or tax records) — minimum necessary amount and retention period

sections.heading: Processing time
paragraphs: We confirm receipt within a few business days and complete deletion within 30 calendar days of verifying your identity. If we need more information, we will email you at the same address.

sections.heading: After deletion
paragraphs: Your account cannot be restored — returning to the platform requires a new registration. If you also used the Telegram bot, disconnect it in Telegram settings or email us and we will unlink the bot from the deleted profile.
